summary.summary: This is the investment-side appendix of Shropshire's treasury outturn report, covering only cash investment strategy and performance for 2025/26, not the council's debt or borrowing position. Bank Rate fell in three 0.25% steps during the year (May, August, December) from 4.50% to 3.75%, and the council's internal treasury team achieved an average return of 4.05% against a SONIA overnight benchmark of 4.19% -- a shortfall of 0.14%, attributed to holding very short-term cash balances for liquidity. At 31 March 2026 the whole £54.2m cash portfolio matured within one month, with nothing held in any longer maturity band. No debt, CFR, borrowing or capital figures appear in this appendix; those would sit in the companion treasury outturn sections not included in this cached document.

compliance.notes: Strong on the technical prudential/treasury indicators and the liability benchmark - a fully-charted 10-year benchmark (LB-01/02 = 3), thorough capex/CFR reconciliation (PI-01/02 = 3), a robust CDS-overlay creditworthiness policy (INV-03 = 3) and a detailed, full-council-approved MRP policy (MRP-02 = 3). Governance and reporting are solid (three-stage Audit&Governance/Cabinet/Council approval, quarterly monitoring, 2021 Codes formally adopted for 2026/27). Weakest areas: (1) the financing-costs-to-net-revenue-stream ratio (PI-07, a CORE affordability indicator) is entirely absent - striking given Shropshire declared a financial emergency on 10 Sep 2025 and its CFR nearly doubles (591m->1,080m) on assumed Exceptional Financial Support; (2) knowledge & skills (KS-01, core) is only a training reference, not a formal policy/schedule; (3) the commercial/non-treasury core items (COM-01 no-borrow-for-yield statement, COM-03 quantified proportionality) are only referenced, and several commercial disclosures (COM-02/07/09) are absent from the documents read - partly because the packet's 'capital strategy' is a 2025/26 in-year review stock-take rather than the full Capital Strategy 2026/27, so the detailed commercial/proportionality disclosures that normally live there could not be evidenced. Also missing: borrowing-in-advance-of-need policy (BOR-02), sterling-borrowing statement (BOR-03), audit-qualification flag (RPT-05) and a derivatives policy (RISK-06).

gaps.evidence: TMSS p.4: financing costs named as an indicator to be split GF/HRA, but no ratio-of-financing-costs-to-net-revenue-stream table or figures anywhere in the TMSS

TMSS p.3-4: commercial initiatives/loans to third parties classed as non-treasury and separated from treasury; low risk appetite (p.2); capstrat requires council-funded capital to 'improve the Council's financial position or be operationally essential'

TMSS p.16 (S151 role): 'ensuring the proportionality of all investments so that the authority does not undertake a level of investing which exposes the authority to an excessive level of risk compared to its financial resources'

news_drafts.headline: Shropshire Council faces widespread control failures as recovery plan unfolds
news_drafts.lead: Shropshire Council is undergoing recovery and transformation following governance and financial difficulties identified in a December 2025 Improvement Plan. An audit of internal controls from April to August found 42 per cent of audit areas received only limited or unsatisfactory assurance, indicating significant control weaknesses. These included payroll problems persisting four years despite repeated interventions, purchase order authorization breaches affecting 386 cases of £125.1m in orders, and schools deficit governance failures, with Bishops Castle's deficit projected to grow to £1m by 2028 despite a recovery plan. However, the pension fund audit found no material misstatements and the fund will continue to meet its obligations to members and employers.
news_drafts.paper_title: SPF Draft 9-107 LGPS Audit Findings Report 2025-26 v2

news_drafts.headline: Shropshire pension fund faces significant cyber oversight gap, auditors warn
news_drafts.lead: An audit of Shropshire's pension fund has identified a gap in cyber security oversight rated "Significant" by the auditors—the only finding at that top priority level among 17 recommendations. The Internal Audit report found that the pension fund and the council's Information and Communications Technology (ICT) team do not hold regular meetings to oversee cyber threats, system changes, and incident management. The auditors recommended that "regular meetings [be] held between the Pension Fund and Shropshire ICT to ensure adequate oversight of cyber threats and risks." The finding was flagged as highest priority because the pension fund systems hold pensioner data and process benefit payments. Six audit recommendations on pensions administration procedures—including outdated policy logs and insufficient payroll controls—were rated as requiring attention.
news_drafts.paper_title: Internal Audit Pension Fund Annual Opinion Report

findings.paper_title: 20260924.25 Shropshire EFS External Assurance Review - Council.Audit
findings.headline: Organisational capacity and leadership are identified as important to supporting financial recovery.
findings.detail: The CIPFA review identified organisational capacity, capability and leadership as important factors in supporting financial recovery. The council recognises the need for continued focus on ensuring it has sufficient workforce capacity and appropriate skills in finance, transformation, programme management, commercial activity and change management.
findings.matters: Even well-designed financial recovery plans fail if the organisation lacks the capacity and capability to execute them; insufficient staffing or skills are material execution risks.
findings.quote: The Review identifies the importance of organisational capacity, capability and leadership in supporting the Council's financial recovery and long-term sustainability.

findings.paper_title: 20260924.25 Shropshire EFS External Assurance Review - Council.Audit
findings.headline: Detailed transformation delivery plans and quantified savings trajectories remain incomplete.
findings.detail: The council acknowledges that several CIPFA recommendations require substantial further work. Specifically, detailed transformation delivery plans, quantified savings trajectories and longer-term financial recovery arrangements remain incomplete. The council identifies this as a key action within its Improvement Plan.
findings.matters: A council's path to financial sustainability depends on detailed, quantified savings plans; their absence indicates significant execution risk and timing uncertainty for financial recovery.
findings.quote: several recommendations remain that require substantial further work – including the further development of detailed transformation delivery plans, quantified savings trajectories and longer-term financial recovery arrangements remain a work in progress.

findings.paper_title: 20260924.25 Shropshire EFS External Assurance Review - Council.Audit
findings.headline: A CIPFA External Assurance Review identified 22 recommendations covering financial management, sustainability, governance and service transformation.
findings.detail: In April 2026, CIPFA undertook an independent review of the council's financial resilience, governance and organisational capacity. The review concluded that significant action is required to achieve financial sustainability and made 22 recommendations. The council acknowledges that while many align with existing improvement activities, several recommendations require substantial further work.
findings.matters: An independent audit of financial resilience by a professional body provides critical evidence of a council's financial health and management capability, essential for lenders assessing recovery prospects.
findings.quote: The Review recognises the scale of the financial challenge facing the Council and concludes that significant action and activity is required if financial sustainability is to be achieved.

findings.paper_title: 20260924.25 Shropshire EFS External Assurance Review - Council.Audit
findings.headline: The council is subject to a Best Value Notice and ongoing government monitoring by MHCLG.
findings.detail: Shropshire Council operates under a Best Value Notice with formal monitoring by MHCLG. The council must provide a formal progress update by end of September 2026, followed by routine quarterly monitoring meetings with government.
findings.matters: Best Value Notices are formal intervention measures issued when government judges a council to have failed its statutory duty; they establish ongoing external oversight.
findings.figures: Progress update deadline: end September 2026; subsequent quarterly meetings
findings.quote: Responding to the CIPFA Review recommendations is a requirement of the EFS arrangements and will be monitored by MHCLG as part of the Best Value Notice process.

findings.paper_title: 20260924.25 Shropshire EFS External Assurance Review - Council.Audit
findings.headline: The council declared a financial emergency in September 2025.
findings.detail: Shropshire Council formally declared a financial emergency in September 2025. This extraordinary step preceded the establishment of an Improvement Plan and strengthened governance structures to address underlying financial issues.
findings.matters: Financial emergencies are rare, formal declarations that signal severe and immediate financial stress requiring unprecedented actions.
findings.quote: following the declaration of a financial emergency in September 2025

daily_post.headline: A structural conflict of interest exists in pension fund governance where Shropshire Council is both administering authority and scheme employer.
daily_post.lead: Unmanaged conflicts of interest in fund governance could compromise independence of pension decisions and expose the council to member challenges, regulator scrutiny, or legal challenge that conflicts were not properly controlled.
